situation: My team won big and played selfish, ugly ball the entire game.

dims.SPEAKABILITY: Card 2's lines flow more naturally out loud, especially "I can coach a team that... I cannot do both," whereas Card 1's "make the people around them dangerous" and the extra-pass inventory exercise feel more constructed.
dims.SPECIFICITY: Card 2's read that "winning validates the selfish approach" and can swallow a team win in personal glory nails the exact danger of this situation, while Card 1's status/belonging framing is sharp but slightly more transferable to any win.
dims.TIGHTNESS: Card 2 is leaner with less redundancy, whereas Card 1 repeats the "makes individual players look elite" idea across both Collaboration and Commitment beats.
dims.HONESTY: Both keep the standard, but Card 2's "what would they say this team is about?" forces the uncomfortable self-examination harder than Card 1's more comforting "that actually makes you look better" reframe.
